notes:
• Mac: smaller download, the disk image is LZMA-compressed (about a third smaller)
• Mac: an experimental chat minimap (Settings → Experimental, off by default). A narrow overview of the whole chat at the right edge, as in VS Code, with tiny thumbnails of its images, to find and jump to a place: click to jump, drag or scroll to move, hover a thumbnail to see it larger. Mac only; the phones lack the width.
• Search in chats: ⌘F (on the phones in the chat's menu) opens a find bar over the chat that marks the messages holding the words, steps through them ("3 of 12") and loads older messages to find more. Search on the Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android gets Messages: every chat's prompts and replies, archived workspaces' too, from a full-text index on the Mac; a hit opens the chat on that message. Search opens with the cursor in its field on the Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android.
• A token per device: the pairing QR code and link carry a one-time code (10 minutes, works once) that the iPhone, Android or another Mac swaps for its own token. Settings → Devices on the Mac lists the paired phones and Macs with when they were paired and last seen, and revokes one without the others; the phones' Settings show the list too. Phones and Macs paired before keep working and switch to their own token by themselves. "Rotate shared token" ends only the pairings still on the old shared token. Older apps can't read the new pairing links: update them first.
• "Fork to new tab", "Fork to new workspace" and "Reset chat" in the "…" under an agent's reply now work, on the Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android: a new chat (or workspace with the files as the turn left them) holding the chat up to that turn, or the chat itself taken back to it after asking, files included, with what was there kept in a checkpoint. Claude chats only for now; Codex chats keep them greyed out.
• Stellwerk for Mac: a guided setup on first start, in five steps. This Mac; Agents: Claude Code and Codex installed and signed in from the app (one is enough); Accounts: GitHub (sign in with a device code and the workflow scope, git uses that login, git's name and email from GitHub) and Entire; Phone: QR code, Tailscale and Serve, ticked off once a phone connects; Projects: import from Conductor or add one from GitHub or a folder. Settings → Advanced → Run setup again shows it again. The GitHub CLI now comes with Stellwerk (a gh of your own wins), so agents have gh without Homebrew. Reading Conductor's projects also works when its database can't be opened read-only. On Mac, iPhone and Android the project toggle now reads "Team chats for this project (enables Entire)"; otherwise the phone apps don't change.
• Mac: two Lotum color themes (Settings → Appearance), in Lotum's neon #CFFF00. Ayu Lotum: Ayu Dark with the neon for its yellow. Lotum: white and black with neon fills, light and dark, set in Montserrat. Mac window only, like the other themes; the phones keep their own look.
• Mac: changed images open in Changes as before and after (with size), other binary files (PDFs, …) show their content instead of "Binary file". The right panel's tabs open from a "+" menu like t3code's (All files F, Changes C, Checks K; × on a tab closes it), Changes is open by default. New "All files" tab, like Conductor's: the workspace's files as a tree with a filter; a file opens as a tab next to the chats. The host serves files git lists (not ignored ones like `.env`) and a changed file's version at the base (`rev=base`).
• Mac: the right panel's bottom has a "+" after Usage for terminals you can close (×), up to three per workspace, instead of a fixed Terminal tab. An empty Setup or Run tab offers "Ask agent" (a new chat with the prompt ready, you add what you want) and "Add manually" (the project's settings).
• Stellwerk for Mac: a terminal. Terminals at the right panel's bottom: your shell in the workspace's folder with the scripts' variables. The host runs them, so they keep going when the window closes; archiving a workspace ends them, and asks first (on the Mac, iPhone and Android) while a program like `claude` still runs in one. Mac only, the phones have no terminals.
• iPhone, iPad, Android: the app shows the last known workspaces and the 20 chats opened last at once on a cold start, without network or while the Mac sleeps, then loads as usual. If loading fails, a notice says "Offline · showing what was there at 10:42". Not in the Mac window.
• New in the Mac's Usage tab: "Continue when limits reset". When Claude's limits stop a turn and no account has room left, the chat carries on by itself a minute after they reset. The chat shows "Resumes at 14:05" with a Cancel button, on the Mac, iPhone and Android.
• Stellwerk for Mac: import projects from Superset (Paradev), in the setup's Projects step and Settings → Advanced → Import projects from Superset. Each picked project gets its own clone in ~/stellwerk/repos with the .env files of its folder, like the Conductor import; Superset's workspaces and your folders stay as they are. "Team chats for this project (enables Entire)" now starts unticked everywhere: both imports and Add project on Mac, iPhone and Android; projects that already have Entire keep it. The import itself is Mac only.
• A queue you can see and edit: follow-ups sent with queue wait in a tray above the message box, numbered, instead of as faded bubbles in the chat. Send one now (it steers the running turn), edit it in place, remove it or reorder it (Mac: drag handle; iPhone: swipe, "…" or long-press drag; Android: "…" or long-press drag). The queue lives on the Mac, so every app shows the same one, and it survives a restart. After Stop it waits ("Paused · sends after your next message") instead of starting right away. While the agent works, sending now queues by default on the Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android; Send now (⌘↩, holding the phones' send button, or the button that stays on the message queued last) puts it right into the turn. The Mac's Settings → General can switch back to steering.
• Watch pull requests: a switch in Settings → Git on the Mac (off by default). When a workspace's PR has failing checks, new review comments from others or a merge conflict, its most recent chat gets the matching prompt (Fix errors, Address comments, Resolve conflicts) once all its chats are idle; each event once, at most 3 times an hour per workspace.
• Work on a PR: "Start from" above a new workspace's first message picks a pull request or a remote branch instead of a fresh branch off the base (open PRs with filters Mine and Drafts, search, checks, Draft, Has workspace; or the remote branches); the workspace is made on that branch with the PR in the git bar, or the workspace already on it opens. On the Mac the project's "+" now opens a draft workspace (a "New workspace" row, × to discard) with the normal message box: the worktree and setup script start only when the first message is sent ("Create without message" in the "Start from" menu for an empty one). iPhone, iPad and Android: the "+" opens "New workspace" with the same control. PRs from forks are refused with a message; older Macs don't show "Start from".
• Sturdier agents and connections. Stopping or ending a chat now also ends what its agent started (MCP servers, background shells), and agents end with Stellwerk even when it crashes. Very long agent output no longer slows the host down. Transcripts load gzipped (much less data over Tailscale), no change notice gets lost when a phone reads slowly, a message sent over a flaky connection is tried again and sent only once, and the apps reconnect right away after switching between Wi-Fi and cellular. The Usage tab shows Codex's limits too, Claude's come from /usage's structured report, and branch names come as structured output.
• "Start from" → Branches lists the remote branches again instead of "No other branches".
• Stellwerk stays responsive with many workspaces running. Mac: the window no longer loses its connection to its own host after you look at a few workspaces with a terminal open. A terminal that's off screen stops streaming its output and picks up where it left off when shown again, and streams no longer use up the connections other requests need. Archiving takes seconds even for big workspaces: the folder is moved aside and deleted in the background, so archiving no longer fails with "git worktree failed (15)". If GitHub returns an error (such as a 502) for a merge that went through anyway, the merge counts as done. The apps wait long enough for Merge, Pull, Push and Archive. Turn checkpoints read only the files that changed. Pull request polling fetches each repository's target branch once instead of once per workspace, and runs a few workspaces at a time. If a git tool hangs, it no longer blocks one of the host's threads; at its timeout the tool and everything it started are stopped. When the host stops answering, the host log names the part that hangs.
• Mac: the right panel's Changes shows the spinner while loading instead of an earlier "Couldn’t load changes", and tries again after 4 s when loading failed.
• Stellwerk for Mac: "Use the account with the most of its week left" now switches only when the active Claude account's limits run out (its current session or week), not as soon as another account has used 5 points less of its week. Then it asks the other accounts first (a one-word Haiku turn, all at once), so it picks by fresh numbers.
• A `stellwerk://pair` link opened from outside the app (camera, message, web page) now asks "Pair with …?" before pairing, on iPhone, iPad, Android and the Mac. Continuing a teammate's session asks first too, since their branch's setup script and agent hooks then run on your Mac.
• Find in chat (⌘F) puts the cursor in its field reliably on the Mac, iPhone and iPad.
• Mac and Android look for new releases every hour instead of every six hours.
• A screenshot or file pasted into the middle of a message on the Mac stays where it was in the sent message instead of moving to its start (the Mac's host says so in `/api/health`; older hosts keep it in front). Queued messages show their attachments under the text on the Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android.
• iPhone: after turning from landscape back to portrait the chat fits the screen again instead of running off both sides.
• Mac: the right panel's + lists only tabs that aren't open yet and hides when all are open.
• Plan mode: a plan now waits for you instead of going straight into implementing it. The chat ends its turn with the plan and a "Plan ready" card on the Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android: **Approve plan** sends it on out of plan mode, or write what to change.
• Mac: "Start from" → Pull requests shows the filtered list right away when Mine or Drafts is clicked, not only after typing.
• Release review fixes:
• **Queue:** a turn Claude rejects at the limits no longer uses up the queue. "Send now" can't send twice, and the sent prompt no longer disappears from the chat. Reset chat keeps queued prompts and cancels a planned "continue at reset".
• **Security:**
• Watch pull requests only sends review comments by the repo's owners, members and collaborators to the agent by itself.
• Rotate shared token also ends the device tokens apps got for it.
• A revoked device loses its open terminal and file streams too.
• Wrong pairing codes lock out only their source.
• Terminals can't set the clipboard (OSC 52) and open only http(s) links.
• The copied pairing link stays out of clipboard managers.
• **Mac:**
• Right-panel terminals pause off screen, are let go with their workspace, and don't come back as new shells after a restart.
• Switching workspaces no longer puts the cursor in a terminal.
• Drafts close on switching Macs.
• Return in setup's code field no longer skips the step.
• Faster: the window redraws less, All files filters off the main thread, the chat minimap updates less while streaming, and the Usage tab asks at most once a minute.
• **Host:**
• Search indexing and PR watching cost less.
• A failed Codex start no longer leaves a process behind.
• Terminal output to slow clients is bounded.
• **iPhone and Android:**
• Retried sends no longer post twice to older Macs.
• A pairing whose first check fails is kept.
• Find and older pages no longer race the saved chat.
• Network changes reconnect sooner, and the offline copy is written less often.
• Android: dragging in the queue sends the right order, and "Resumes at" shows the date for another day like iPhone.
• Project icons come from the logo on the remote's default branch (`origin/HEAD`) instead of the project folder's checkout, which nobody updates since workspaces are worktrees. Stellwerk's own project showed the old Pocket logo because of that.
• Mac: the scripts panel's tabs (Setup, Run, Usage, terminals) wrap onto a second line when the right panel is too narrow.
• Mac: a terminal keeps its prompt and what was typed after switching workspaces and back.
• Stellwerk for Mac, Usage tab: a Claude | Codex switch at the top, each agent in its own section. "Pick the account with the most of its week left" now sits under "Switch accounts when limits run out" and only says how it picks (on before means switching stays on). Each Claude account gets "Use when switching", so a switch skips the ones you leave out. The stop setting says it only stops once every account is out of room. Codex's limits show without a Codex chat (asked for free on opening the tab, on Refresh and every five minutes).
• Codex chats retry again when the model is at capacity, fast mode is offered for Opus 5 only (Claude Code ends it for Opus 4.8 on November 30), review comments added to a chat can no longer pose as your instructions, and dependencies are up to date.
• iOS: the "…" button in a workspace opens its menu again. The screen kept drawing itself over and over, which used a full CPU core and rebuilt the menu before it could open.
